title: Claude sees only the tools, and the Dev loop names its own next stage

statements.says: implement and to-tickets set disable-model-invocation: true, so Claude no longer sees them.
The driver types /skillworks:implement in each Session, as it did.
The driver now cuts a spec's tickets itself, as a step of its own that types /skillworks:to-tickets.
A developer can still type any of the hidden skills.
The tools, such as tdd and review-changes, stay open to Claude.
to-spec stays open to Claude, and its description points at the Grill instead.
Staying visible with a "Not for" line in its description is kept for to-spec, the one step the Grill has to call through the Skill tool.
Each stage of the Dev loop names only the next stage.
Setup's allowlist opens ~/.claude/plugins/, and a Marketplace folder outside the repo, to reading.
Claude sees the description of every skill it may start, and never the description of a skill that sets disable-model-invocation: true.
Because spec-loop and the Grill set the flag and to-tickets and implement did not, Claude suggested those two after a spec was published and never spec-loop, the one the Dev loop wants.
The driver cuts the tickets itself because nothing may call a hidden skill through the Skill tool.
to-spec stays open because the Grill calls it through the Skill tool.
Three runs of claude -p on 2026-09-28, against a throwaway plugin, decided it.
In those runs, a hidden skill ran when its command was typed.
In those runs, the Skill tool refused to call a hidden skill, and said: "Do not replicate this skill's workflow by other means".
In those runs, a skill that read a hidden skill's file to follow it was refused the read, because the plugin's folder sat outside the repo.
A skill's own extra files were never readable in a loop Session when the Plugin sits outside the repo, as it does in every repo but this one.

Having the calling skill read the hidden skill's file and follow it was rejected, because it works only once a read rule opens the plugin's folder, it goes around what Claude Code means the flag for, which is a skill run only when a person asks, and a later version of Claude Code could close it.

Keeping every flow step visible with a "Not for" line in its description was rejected for implement and to-tickets, because a line of text asks Claude not to suggest them and the flag makes sure it cannot.
